The statement communicates a credible commitment to average inflation targeting (the “makeup strategy” noted by Powell at Jackson Hole 2020), allowing inflation to run moderately above 2% after past undershoots, which should help anchor longer‑run expectations near 2% while lowering real rates via forward guidance. In the New Keynesian policy-rule framework (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), such guidance at the zero lower bound is expansionary and supports employment. The operational details—maintaining the 0–0.25% federal funds range, setting IORB at 0.15%, and using ON RRP/repo—are consistent with the post‑2008 floor system and policy implementation principles discussed by Goodfriend (2002). Continued QE ($80B Treasuries/$40B agency MBS) aligns with the literature on the Fed’s use of balance sheet tools to influence term premia and the mortgage channel, supporting credit to households while overall financial conditions remain accommodative. Balanced against these positives, the Committee underscores virus‑related risks and labels inflation pressures as largely transitory, reflecting a risk‑management stance rather than a Taylor‑principle tightening. Net tone: moderately positive but cautious.
